import pandas as pd

# File paths for source tables
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_42/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_42/training_1.csv"

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Operation History: JOIN on ["item_id", "item_id"]
# Join source0 and source1 on 'item_id' column (inner join by default)
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, how='inner', on='item_id')

# Target schema:
# ['user_id': integer, 'item_id': integer, 'rating': integer, 'timestamp': integer, 'movie title': string]

# Select and rename columns to match target schema exactly
# Columns available after join:
# source0: user_id, item_id, rating, timestamp
# source1: item_id, movie title, release date, video release date, IMDb URL, unknown, Action, Adventure, Animation, Childrens, Comedy, Crime, Documentary, Drama, Fantasy, Film-Noir, Horror, Musical, Mystery, Romance, Sci-Fi, Thriller, War, Western

# We only need: user_id, item_id, rating, timestamp, movie title
target_df = joined[['user_id', 'item_id', 'rating', 'timestamp', 'movie title']].copy()

# Ensure data types match target schema
target_df['user_id'] = target_df['user_id'].astype(int)
target_df['item_id'] = target_df['item_id'].astype(int)
target_df['rating'] = target_df['rating'].astype(int)
target_df['timestamp'] = target_df['timestamp'].astype(int)
target_df['movie title'] = target_df['movie title'].astype(str)

# Write the result to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_42/target_multisource.csv"
target_df.to_csv(target_path, index=False)
